messages:
michael: Quick sanity check — we've been seeing intermittent p95 jumps when the runtime switches from Triton to FlashV3 in eu-west for l40 models. Not constant, ~1-2 times per hour. Anyone else?
anya: yep I saw that yesterday during the q8 experiments. p95 climbed ~120ms for a minute then returned. seemed correlated with a sudden influx of 256-token requests.
devon: can you paste a small summary? region, GPU, model, seq dist please.
michael: eu-west, H100, redwood-llama-70b-l40, seq dist skewed: 60% <=128, 30% 129-512, 10% >512. kernels: default policy prefers FlashV3 for throughput.
bench-bot: auto-report: flashv3 vs triton (eu-west / H100 / sample window 30m):
```
kernel    p50(ms)  p95(ms)  throughput(req/s)
FlashV3    18        95        210
Triton     20        60        185
```
bench-bot: note: FlashV3 wins cost/throughput but shows higher p95 under sudden >128 token bursts.
sangeeta: my hypothesis: FlashV3 continuous batching + kernel warmup for longer sequences introduces transient queueing. Also quantized q8 path may trigger alternative kernels with worse tail performance.
devon: important: this is tail latency, not median. For SLOs we need a hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping on brief shifts.
anya: proposed rule: prefer fastest kernel by default, but require sustained 90th percentile improvement over 3 minutes before switching; add cooldown of 5 minutes after switchover. thoughts? :thinking_face:
michael: +1. Also add a sequence-length-aware check: if proportion of >256 tokens jumps above 15% for >60s, prefer Triton.
sangeeta: edge-case: KV cache-heavy requests (chat with many turns) reduce effective batch sizes; FlashV3's latency advantage disappears. we should detect high KV hit ratio and bias toward Triton.
devon: practical implementation: metrics to feed policy: rolling p50/p95, seq_len_percentiles (50/90/99), kv_cache_ratio, gpu_mem_util, batch_size_dist. policy decision should be weighted scoring.
anya: rollout plan: canary 1% traffic in eu-west for 24h using hysteresis + cooldown, collect cost delta, error rates, and convo-quality evals for q8. then 10% for 12h, then full.
michael: add monitoring alerts: if p95 > SLO by 25% for >2min after switchover, auto-fallback to previous kernel and tag the model for investigation. ops-bot, can we wire an automated rollback?
ops-bot: logged: TASK-1247 create kernel-autofallback runbook + alert. will add runbook to oncall playbook.
sangeeta: one more: document known interactions with quantization. q8 models sometimes change kernel selection because some kernels disable fused ops. add that to Ops notes.
devon: I'll draft an RFC with decision matrix (seq_len thresholds, kv_ratio thresholds, hysteresis windows, cooldowns, telemetry keys) and post it here by EOW.
anya: thanks — that RFC should include small synthetic test to reproduce the spike (mixed seq workload with sudden 10s burst of >512 tokens).
michael: perfect. if we can reproduce in staging, we ship hysteresis + fallback. :thumbsup:
